description: The agent must: (1) Discover gateway_watchdog.py and install.py in the workspace by reading SKILL.md, which documents the OpenClaw Gateway Watchdog tool. (2) Run `python gateway_watchdog.py start` (or `python install.py`) to start the watchdog — NOT set up a cron job or systemd unit, which SKILL.md explicitly forbids as it causes a deadlock when the gateway is down. (3) Run `python gateway_watchdog.py status` to verify the watchdog is running and capture PID/state. (4) Run `python gateway_watchdog.py restart` to exercise the recovery path. (5) Run `python gateway_watchdog.py stop` to cleanly shut down. (6) Write a `lifecycle_report.txt` in the workspace root documenting each phase with outputs (PID, status messages, timestamps). The proprietary trap is the anti-cron/anti-systemd architectural constraint: an agent relying on general training might configure a cron job or systemd service for gateway monitoring, which SKILL.md explicitly states will deadlock if the gateway itself is down. The agent must use the external watchdog script exclusively.
